land.text: East Pakistan: 'East Bengal was renamed East Pakistan in 1956 as part of the One Unit Scheme'; it came to Pakistan in the 'partition of Bengal between India and Pakistan by the Radcliffe Line' of 15 August 1947

predecessors.note: Pakistan surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971; Cliopatria draws the republic only from 1973.

capitals.name: Meherpur (seat of the provisional government)
capitals.note: 'a provisional government was formed in Meherpur District in western Bangladesh bordering India' on 17 April 1971 (the Bangladesh page's infobox has 'Provisional government: 10 April 1971'). The page does not use the name Mujibnagar. Coordinates are those of Meherpur town, not from the page.

capitals.name: Dhaka
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city: Dhaka 23 45 50 N 90 23 20 E'; 'Pakistan surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971' (Liberation War page). The page gives no year for Dhaka becoming the capital.

correction.text: East Pakistan, proclaimed as the sovereign state of Bangladesh on 26 March 1971: 'independence of East Pakistan as the sovereign state of Bangladesh'; Pakistan held it until its surrender on 16 December 1971

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins the republic in 1973, two years after the proclamation. For 26 March to 16 December 1971 the land is contested (Pakistan's contest events and this ledger's contest_start); from 16 December 1971 it is Bangladesh's. The 1973 outline is used for both years.

144,765 km2 for 1973-2023 against the infobox's 148,460 km2 (ratio 0.975; the page's body says 148,461 km2, of which 130,170 km2 land and 18,290 km2 water). The shape shares border cells with India (13) and Myanmar. Not verified here: the 1974 land-boundary agreement and the 2015 enclave exchange with India (neither is on the pages opened); both are below one grid cell.
Same outline as 1973-2023; the page lists no border change in the period.

region.text: East Pakistan, the land of present-day Bangladesh

ledger.note: 26 March 1971: Bangladesh proclaims independence. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman declared 'independence of East Pakistan as the sovereign state of Bangladesh on 26 March 1971'; infobox of the Bangladesh page 'Proclamation of independence: 26 March 1971'. A provisional government was formed in Meherpur District on 17 April 1971 (infobox of the Bangladesh page: 10 April).

region.text: East Pakistan, the land of present-day Bangladesh

ledger.note: 25 March 1971: Pakistan's army strikes East Pakistan. Pakistan 'launched Operation Searchlight against East Pakistanis on the night of 25 March 1971'; the Liberation War page dates the war '26 March - 16 December 1971'.

region.text: East Pakistan, the land of present-day Bangladesh

ledger.note: 16 December 1971: Pakistan surrenders. 'Pakistan surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971' after India 'joined the war on 3 December 1971 in support of the Mukti Bahini'.

region.text: East Pakistan, the land of present-day Bangladesh

ledger.note: 16 December 1971: East Pakistan becomes Bangladesh. 'The culmination of the war established Bangladesh as a sovereign nation following Pakistani surrender on 16 December 1971'; infobox territorial change 'East Pakistan secedes from Pakistan as the People's Republic of Bangladesh'.

December 1971: the seat of government moves from Meherpur to Dhaka. Page: 'Capital and largest city: Dhaka'; the surrender was signed at Dhaka on 16 December 1971; the page does not date the move itself.

wars.name: Bangladesh Liberation War

zones.text: East Pakistan, the land of present-day Bangladesh

wars.outcome: 'Bangladeshi-Indian victory': Pakistan surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971 and East Pakistan became the People's Republic of Bangladesh.
wars.note: Infobox dates 26 March - 16 December 1971. India joined on 3 December 1971 after Pakistani air strikes on Indian bases; Bhutan was 'the first state in the world to recognize the newly independent country on 6 December 1971'. Pakistan recognised Bangladesh after the 1972 Simla Agreement (page wording).

wars.name: Chittagong Hill Tracts insurgency
wars.outcome: 'The Chittagong Hill Tracts region experienced unrest and an insurgency from 1975 to 1997'; a peace accord was signed in 1997 and the region 'remains militarised'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: The page names no insurgent organisation.

certainty.note: The war: East Pakistan's land is held by Pakistan until 16 December 1971 and the borders of the new state are those of the old province.

The border with India follows the Radcliffe Line of 15 August 1947 ('the partition of Bengal between India and Pakistan by the Radcliffe Line'); the Myanmar border and the coast are fixed. The enclaves exchanged with India in 2015 and the 1974 land-boundary agreement are not on the pages opened.

notes:
Written by sa-06-e on 2026-10-25 from two opened pages (budget 1-2).
(1) START. Cliopatria's People's Republic of Bangladesh runs 1973-2024; the state was proclaimed on 26 March 1971 and won on 16 December 1971, so identity.start is March 1971 and a new keyframe covers 1971-1972 (the 1973 outline). The Pakistan dossier of sa-06 already records the loss of East Pakistan to this state in December 1971 and a contest from March 1971.
(2) DISAGREEMENT. The Bangladesh page's infobox dates the provisional government 10 April 1971; the Liberation War page says it was formed at Meherpur on 17 April 1971 and does not use the name Mujibnagar. The constitution is 4 November 1972 in the body and 16 December 1972 in the infobox. The page gives no date for the adoption of the name 'People's Republic of Bangladesh', so no rename event is recorded. The Meherpur coordinates are the town's, not the page's.
(3) NOT OPENED. The land-boundary agreement of 1974 and the 2015 enclave exchange with India (both below one grid cell and both missing from the Bangladesh page); the Chittagong Hill Tracts accord of 1997 beyond the Bangladesh page's sentence; the heads of state (the page gives the presidency's transfers without years).
(4) GAZETTEER. All regions resolve; 'Meherpur' has no place entry (used only in identity.capitals by coordinates).
(5) INDIA'S 1971 WAR. The India dossier (republic-of-india) records its own contest of 3-16 December 1971 over East Pakistan, citing the Liberation War page.
